描述_ZN: Tiger" scroll, modern, painted by Qi Baishi, on paper, color, 68 cm in length and 33.6 cm in width.　　This painting breaks with the traditional method of painting a tiger facing the viewer with a frontal image, and only depicts the back of the tiger. However, through the twisting figure of the tiger's back, one can still feel the robustness and strength of its body, and although the autumn grasses on both sides of the tiger's body are swaying, one can still feel its kingly demeanor of not being moved by its surroundings and being the only one.　　It was Mr. Qi Baishi's consistent artistic idea to draw his own true feelings and to set new standards. For this reason, he carved a seal of "I make my own paintings" to show that in his artistic creation, he not only taught himself to the ancients and the creators, but also paid more attention to innovation and change to shape his own style. He once admonished his disciples: "Those who learn from me live, those who resemble me die", asking them to be like the gods and not like the forms, rather than simply inheriting the teachings of the master, otherwise his art would be lifeless. Mr. Qi Baishi is most known for his paintings of fruits and vegetables, flowers, figures, and fish, shrimps, and crabs, but his paintings of tigers are extremely rare.　　This painting is signed: "Made by Qi Juan, a rich man with three hundred stone seals", with the inscription "Qi Da" in vermilion, and was acquired in the Palace Museum in Beijing in 1957.
